text.p: Argentina's labor ministry said 30.9 percent of Argentines have joined in Thursday's general, according to state news agency Telam.

The highest proportion of strikers, of 55.7 percent, was in the central Argentine province of Cordoba while the lowest was in the north-western province of La Rioja, where only 0.4 percent of workers stayed at home.
In the capital Buenos Aires, 41 percent of workers were on strike.
Defense Minister Jorge Dominquez said earlier Thursday the "turnout is 50 percent less than in the last stoppage," in September.
Rodolfo Daer, meanwhile, the head of Argentina's main CGT labor federation called the strike a "success." A 36-hour strike in September had a 90 percent turnout according to unions.

The walkout, the third general strike this year, was called by unions to protest three decrees on labor market reforms signed by President Carlos Menem last week. Unlike the other strikes however, no marches nor protests were called for this time.
